name: Ahijah
overview: Ahijah was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, identified specifically as being from the house of Issachar. He is noted primarily for his paternal relationship to Baasha. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahijah means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element referencing the LORD. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges a brotherly relationship with the divine name YHWH.
familyAndRelationships: Ahijah is recorded as the father of Baasha, a relationship inferred from Scripture. He is also explicitly identified as a descendant of Issachar, linking him to the tribe of Issachar. Beyond these, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for Ahijah.
scriptureSignificance: Ahijah's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily through his role as the father of Baasha, who became a notable figure in Israel's history. His tribal affiliation with Issachar situates him within the broader context of Israel's tribal structure. While little else is recorded about him, his mention establishes a genealogical foundation important for understanding the lineage of Baasha.
